Theorem
[local rigidity of constant curvature]

Source: petersen:page-0211 ↗ rem:pet-ch5-hessian-r-asymptotics 1. ch5:5.5.8If a Riemannian $n$-manifold $(M,g)$ has constant sectional curvature $k$, every point of $M$ has a neighborhood isometric to an open subset of the space form $S^n_k$.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch5-riemann-constant-curvature-local \sketch In exponential coordinates, constant curvature gives the radial Riccati equation $ abla _{\partial _r}\operatorname {Hess}r+(\operatorname {Hess}r)^2=-kg_r$, with the asymptotics from subsection 5.3. The model tensor $(\mathrm{sn}_k'/\mathrm{sn}_k)g_r$ satisfies the same equation because

egin{align*} abla _{\partial _r}\! \left( rac{\mathrm{sn}_k'}{\mathrm{sn}_k}g_r ight) +\left( rac{\mathrm{sn}_k'}{\mathrm{sn}_k} ight)^2g_r & =\left( rac{\mathrm{sn}_k'}{\mathrm{sn}_k} ight)’g_r +\left( rac{\mathrm{sn}_k'}{\mathrm{sn}_k} ight)^2g_r + rac{\mathrm{sn}_k'}{\mathrm{sn}_k} abla _{\partial _r}g_r\ & =-kg_r- rac{\mathrm{sn}_k'}{\mathrm{sn}_k} abla _{\partial _r}dr^2=-kg_r, \end{align*}

The prescribed initial behavior and ODE uniqueness yield $\operatorname {Hess}r=(\mathrm{sn}_k'/\mathrm{sn}_k)g_r$. Consequently

\[ f_k(r)= egin{cases} frac 12r^2,& k=0\ frac 1k- frac 1k\mathrm{cs}_k(r),& k e 0\end{cases} \]

satisfies $\operatorname {Hess}f_k=(1-kf_k)g$, using $f_k'=\mathrm{sn}_k$ and $f_k''=\mathrm{cs}_k=1-kf_k$. The local classification for this Hessian equation identifies the metric with the space form $S_k^n$.
